findings.highlight: being utterly powerless to oppose.
findings.evidenceJa: 異を唱える資格などない自分
findings.governingReading: 資格などない concerns his right to object after accepting the lethal contest.
findings.explanation: Lack of ethical standing becomes physical powerlessness.

findings.highlight: I was knocked down without resisting.
findings.evidenceJa: 力任せに倒された
findings.governingReading: 力任せに describes Saber’s force; the next sentence specifies a several-meter throw.
findings.explanation: The attacker’s full force becomes the victim’s nonresistance.

findings.highlight: Saber armoring up.
findings.evidenceJa: 武装したセイバー
findings.governingReading: 武装した describes the equipped Saber he sees.
findings.explanation: Already armed Saber is still armoring up.

findings.highlight: Because of that, she can barely catch her breath.
findings.evidenceJa: おかげでまともに息ができない
findings.governingReading: The collision leaves the narrator unable to breathe normally.
findings.explanation: Shirou’s breathlessness is assigned to Saber.

findings.highlight: she barely has enough strength to even face me.
findings.evidenceJa: 俺を相手にする力さえ残っていない
findings.governingReading: She has not even enough strength left to face him.
findings.explanation: Insufficient strength becomes barely sufficient strength.

findings.highlight: he has answered my one-sided wish.
findings.evidenceJa: 私の一方的な誓いに応えてくれた
findings.governingReading: 誓い is the pledge he answered despite knowing nothing of the War.
findings.explanation: Her one-sided oath becomes her wish.

findings.highlight: The old Saber would've undoubtedly overpowered Archer
findings.evidenceJa: かつてアーチャーを圧倒したセイバー
findings.governingReading: かつて圧倒した recalls what she previously did to Archer.
findings.explanation: Earlier overwhelming victory becomes a hypothetical old-Saber victory.

findings.highlight: If you mimic someone long enough
findings.evidenceJa: 人真似もそこまで行けば本物
findings.governingReading: そこまで行けば concerns the achieved extent of the exact mimicry just observed.
findings.explanation: Degree of imitation becomes duration of imitation.

findings.highlight: paying the price for performing miracles until this point
findings.evidenceJa: おまえをここまで生かしてきた魔術の代償
findings.governingReading: The magic specifically kept him alive up to this point.
findings.explanation: The cost of life-preserving magic becomes the cost of performing miracles generally.

findings.highlight: If this man is truly the same person who wanted to become stronger
findings.evidenceJa: 衛宮士郎の理想に他ならないとしたら
findings.governingReading: The condition names the man as Shirou’s desired ideal, without explicitly equating their personal identities.
findings.explanation: Embodiment of an ideal becomes the same person in the conditional.

findings.highlight: slowly withering away
findings.evidenceJa: ズタズタに崩れよう
findings.governingReading: ズタズタに崩れよう describes violent internal breakdown nearing collapse.
findings.explanation: Imminent shredded collapse becomes slow withering.

findings.highlight: My will creates your body, and your sword creates my destiny!
findings.evidenceJa: 汝の身は我が下に、我が命運は汝の剣に
findings.governingReading: The body is under the summoner; the summoner’s fate rests in the sword.
findings.explanation: Contractual subordination and entrusted fate become creation.

findings.highlight: What are you going do?
findings.evidenceJa: 貴方こそどうするのです
findings.governingReading: Saber asks what Archer will do.
findings.explanation: Going do lacks to.

findings.highlight: with utmost power and precision
findings.evidenceJa: おそらくは最大の力
findings.governingReading: おそらく qualifies the strength estimate; precision is not specified.
findings.explanation: Probable maximum force becomes stated utmost power and precision.

findings.highlight: The magical energy embued in Saber's sword
findings.evidenceJa: セイバーの剣に籠められた魔力
findings.governingReading: The same sword name 干将 appears as “Kanshou” on page 72 and “Kashou” on page 99. The other two anchors contain ordinary English spelling errors.
findings.explanation: The same sword is called “Kanshou” and later “Kashou.” This is a small name-spelling inconsistency; the other two misspellings concern ordinary words.

findings.highlight: Saber stops for a short moment, then swings down her sword.
findings.evidenceJa: 止めとばかりに剣を降り落とす
findings.governingReading: 止めとばかりに means as if delivering the coup de grace.
findings.explanation: A finishing blow becomes a pause.

findings.highlight: impossible for an Archer-class Servant to win against a Saber-class Servant.
findings.evidenceJa: アーチャーがセイバーに勝利する事はあり得ない
findings.governingReading: The narration compares the two fighters just shown struggling unequally. Later, Archer invokes his designation to explain that he is not fundamentally a sword fighter.
findings.explanation: A comparison between these two combatants becomes a rule about Archer- and Saber-class Servants. Archer's later description of himself likewise becomes a claim about all archers' preferences; the dialogue may be rhetorical, but its scope is broader.

findings.highlight: a unique skill that let them stay manifested independently.
findings.evidenceJa: 単独で存在する能力
findings.governingReading: The relative clause modifies one skill.
findings.explanation: Singular skill takes let.

findings.highlight: I'm sure I will be part of it
findings.evidenceJa: おそらくは次も、おまえと関わるのは私なのだろうよ
findings.governingReading: おそらく and だろう mark the expected future relationship as conjecture.
findings.explanation: Probable next involvement becomes I’m sure.

findings.highlight: standing in the middle of this wasted kingdom, is the red knight.
findings.evidenceJa: 赤い騎士は君臨していた
findings.governingReading: 君臨 supplies dominion in the kingdom image, beyond central location.
findings.explanation: Reigning over the rubble kingdom becomes merely standing in it.

findings.highlight: not only were you not a swordsman nor a bowman.
findings.evidenceJa: 剣士でもなければ弓兵でもなくて
findings.governingReading: The unfinished inference excludes both sword and bow roles before Archer supplies mage.
findings.explanation: Not only is joined to nor without its required continuation.

findings.highlight: it categorizes as a weapon
findings.evidenceJa: 武器であるのならば
findings.governingReading: The object belongs to the weapon category.
findings.explanation: Categorizes as lacks passive construction.

findings.highlight: I probably won't survive after Projecting a sacred sword.
findings.evidenceJa: 聖剣など投影しては自滅する
findings.governingReading: Archer states that projecting the sacred sword would destroy him.
findings.explanation: Self-destruction becomes probable nonsurvival.

findings.highlight: You won't die if you're lucky.
findings.evidenceJa: 運が良ければ即死する事もない
findings.governingReading: Luck may prevent immediate death, leaving injury for later healing.
findings.explanation: Avoiding instant death becomes avoiding death.

findings.highlight: strikes down each and every sword that rains down.
findings.evidenceJa: その全てを、手にした剣だけで払いのけようと
findings.governingReading: 払いのけようと marks her aim when facing the attack with mortal resolve.
findings.explanation: An attempt to repel every sword becomes successful deflection of every sword.

findings.highlight: the flurry of swords
findings.evidenceJa: 飛び交う十八の剣
findings.governingReading: 十八 specifies the set he analyzes.
findings.explanation: The analyzed volley loses its eighteen-sword count.

findings.highlight: what I need to do now is let my senses take over and analyze them.
findings.evidenceJa: 肉眼では追い付かず感覚が暴走し
findings.governingReading: The eyes cannot keep up with analysis and the senses run out of control.
findings.explanation: Sensory overrun becomes a deliberate coping strategy.

findings.highlight: You might think highly of that boy
findings.evidenceJa: いかにおまえが小僧を守ろうと
findings.governingReading: いかに守ろうと concerns her attempted protection competing with her Master’s life.
findings.explanation: Protecting Shirou becomes thinking highly of him.

findings.highlight: I am fading in and out of my consciousness.
findings.evidenceJa: 視界が点滅する
findings.governingReading: 視界が点滅する describes the visual field flashing.
findings.explanation: Flickering vision becomes intermittent consciousness.

findings.highlight: I fell down on my knee before I can see him leave.
findings.evidenceJa: 床に膝をついた
findings.governingReading: He sinks to one knee without seeing the departure through.
findings.explanation: Fell before I can mixes the event tenses.
